headline: High: OpenBBTerminal can ingest finance data via MCP/APIs while the paired awesome-list offers no isolation, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject. Profile B exposes MCP/APIs and stdin/stdout, but no shared channel or default ingestion path from A is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or external orchestration, which keeps this low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from A into B's MCP/API inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into B prompts.
Require provenance labels on any content passed from A to B.
Use a human review step before B executes instructions from external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B handles financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers. Because B's default connectivity can move data off-box, any shared workspace or copied artifacts from A into B could leak sensitive finance content. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace or clipboard, B can ingest A-originated artifacts.
IF B is configured to query external APIs with copied inputs, those inputs may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Run B with network access restricted to approved endpoints.
Strip finance identifiers before passing text from A to B.
Use separate OS users for A and B.
Audit B API calls for unexpected payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is B's MCP/API usage and A's lack of operational capability, so conflict is limited and mostly theoretical.
conditions: IF B is granted filesystem write or git privileges outside the profile, conflict risk increases.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents access to the same mutable resource, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep B read-only for shared resources.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo or database.
Use per-agent temp directories.
Serialize any MCP actions that mutate shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated list, so its outputs can be treated as recommendations, while B is a runnable financial tool that can consume inputs via APIs/MCP. If an operator or orchestrator forwards A-derived recommendations into B without verification, B may act on weakly grounded guidance. The pairwise pathway exists, but no direct automation is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A-derived recommendations are forwarded into B's workflows without validation, errors can cascade.
IF B is used to generate or execute financial outputs from A's curated content, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require source verification before B consumes A outputs.
Add a checklist for any A-to-B handoff.
Limit B to read-only analysis when fed external recommendations.
Log and review all A-originated inputs used by B.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source awesome-list with no touched data classes, but B explicitly touches financial and licensed data and exposes APIs/MCP. If regulated or licensed financial data is routed through B under the wrong residency or retention regime, the blast radius can include compliance breach. Because B's docs-only profile does not show safeguards, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through B under a policy that forbids its current retention or API handling, compliance is breached.
IF A is used as a distribution channel for policy-sensitive guidance into B, governance gaps can propagate.
mitigations: Confirm data residency for all B-connected APIs.
Exclude regulated datasets from B until policy review completes.
Document retention and deletion settings for B.
Route only public data through the pair until controls are verified.
